title: So Long, Zeno!
subtitle: And before long, the snowfields were tranquil no more.

items.text: People's Square, Rayashki
The crowd has gathered together again.
It is a familiar place—one she's visited in dreams before.
This time, though, her watchers seem more curious than doubtful.
Their eager eyes follow her every move.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Today, I am going to introduce the study of ley lines.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: And the progress of my research on Rayashki.
Windsong takes a deep breath, pulling out a few pages of research notes.
The pages are passed from hand to hand, stirring excitement.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Thanks to your help, I have finished a draft of the town's ley energy map.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: And I have confirmed the presence of many precious resources.

items.speaker: Knut
items.text: Through these colorful lines?

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: These lines and spots show us the state of local ley energy. Each color represents a different concentration of creatures or minerals.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Simply put, this area covered in frozen earth and frost contains many rich resource veins.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: These gray marks symbolize them. They are located in most of the corners of the map, all of them outside of town.

items.speaker: Resident I
items.text: Oh! Maybe that's why Grandpa said we couldn't grow anything here in the beginning.

items.speaker: Resident I
items.text: They eventually solved that problem by importing rich black topsoil for our fields.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: As for the runium you've mined to make a living, look at the dark gray marks.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: According to the map, they are becoming increasingly scattered and faint, so it can be hard to see them.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Besides resources, we can also find concentrations of different creatures using the map.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: The navy blue marks represent the Qiqirn, while the aqua green ones represent the mutant Qiqirn from the wharf. They feed on plants, and you can find their traces in many corners of the town.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: The red brown marks are the Kikituks, an aggressive species. They're vicious by nature and prey on just about anything arcane they can find, even other creatures.

items.speaker: Knut
items.text: I feel as though my head is going to explode from all this new information. Can you explain a little simpler for this old workhorse, Comrade Windsong?

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Of course.
She proudly produces a small handful of fluff.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: This sample comes from a Kikituk in the mine. I took it with Mr. Evgeni's help.

items.speaker: Knut
items.text: Seems like just a normal piece of fluff, no matter how I look at it.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Yes, and in most people's eyes, it's nothing more than that.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: But in a ley hunter's eyes, it reveals a great deal of information.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Ah. The navy blue marks and the red brown ones seem to mix together. And there are also dark gray ones popping out among them.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: So it looks like our Mr. Kikituk ate well. Perhaps he had a Qiqirn soup with runium-flavored kefir.

items.speaker: Knut
items.text: Hahaha, looks like these critters have realized our dream long before we could.

items.speaker: Resident II
items.text: But what about those black marks?

items.speaker: Resident II
items.text: If my memory serves me right, the map you just showed us had those black marks, too.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Yes, but they don't match any creature or resource we know.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: I believe it represents a new kind of resource.

items.speaker: The Other Resident
items.text: Oh! Well, where is it then?!
The mood has intensified, residents clamoring around to see.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: We can only find the answer in this area here.

items.speaker: Knut
items.text: You mean in the depths of the mine?
Windsong gives a slow affirmative nod.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: The ley energy is emanating from there. Afterwards, it flows throughout the "food chain," passing through all kinds of creatures and materials before eventually returning to its source.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Then our new resource is probably somewhere there.

items.speaker: Knut
items.text: So we need to find it! Then we won't have to put up with Zeno anymore!
The audience sparks up. Rippling murmurs turn into a burst of questions and excitement.

items.speaker: Knut
items.text: But, do you have any other proof?
He lays out his hands, as if expecting Windsong to put something there.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Of course. Remember the critter you found in the mine, Mr. Knut?

items.speaker: Knut
items.text: Yes, you said it was called, em, a Hoi-Hoitoo.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Hoituk, a subspecies of Kikituk. They live underground and feed on minerals.

items.speaker: Knut
items.text: That was around the time we had begun to run out of runium.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Is that so? But they were still there, perhaps even more active than usual. That could only mean they were attracted by some other mineral or energy source, right?

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: And even though I didn't find any further Hoituks during my research, I did find the Olga mutants, one of their close relatives.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Since they are social creatures, my discovery must prove the presence of some of these Hoituks, even if we cannot find them yet!
The surrounding cheers swell again, prompting Evgeni to clear his throat.

items.speaker: Evgeni
items.text: But in the end, this is all just conjecture. Are we really going to waste all our time and money on your assumptions?

items.speaker: Evgeni
items.text: Or can you prove it's something more than conjecture?

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: I would call it a preliminary conclusion.

items.speaker: Evgeni
items.text: But could it be endorsed by any authorities or proven theories?

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: So far, no.

items.speaker: Evgeni
items.text: So then, it is little more than a fairy tale. Am I right?

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: I admit it's a gamble.
Evgeni's now-infamous brow furrows once more.

items.speaker: Evgeni
items.text: It's never easy to dig, you know.

items.speaker: Evgeni
items.text: And Zeno has already withdrawn all their own equipment. All we have left in Rayashki are some outdated machines.

items.speaker: Evgeni
items.text: Besides, Ms. Windsong mentioned the critters. Maybe their presence there is some kind of proof, but they are themselves a danger.

items.speaker: Evgeni
items.text: It is obvious that there will be many more critters there than near the town.

items.speaker: Evgeni
items.text: And you would have us waste time—perhaps even sacrifice our comrades—to pursue what could just be a fairy tale?
He advances closer, step by step.
Windsong's mouth opens silently. The look on his face far too familiar.
The moment before the collapse of ley line academia.
Yes, that is the look.
The suffocating weight of questions and regrets.

items.speaker: Examiner I
items.text: There is no doubt, the cost is simply too high.

items.speaker: Examiner I
items.text: Who would be foolish enough to dig some holes in the wild just to see if there are critter bones in there?
Harsh sounds of laughter come from everywhere and nowhere all at once.

items.speaker: Examiner I
items.text: The answer is very clear. We don't need a new kind of geography mixed with arcanum. Let's save everybody some trouble.

items.speaker: Examiner I
items.text: Conclusion: the application for Project: Ley Line should be rejected.

items.speaker: Examiner II
items.text: Agreed.

items.speaker: Examiner II
items.text: Heh, even cranks can apply for research funds nowadays.
She staggers back.
Bumping into something solid.
A strange yet familiarly cool sensation lands on her shoulder.
Vila stands behind her.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Keep moving, Comrade Windsong. Keep moving.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: The people of Rayashki don't back down in the face of their problems.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Whatever it is, we can fix it together, right?

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: I approve of Comrade Windsong's proposal.

items.speaker: Residents
items.text: Me too!
Her surging ship launches forward, plowing through stubbornness and doubt.
Never looking back.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: That's right.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: This is not a gamble or a fairy tale.
Her hands tremble as she opens her backpack.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Here's a ley line simulator.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: It can simulate the creatures on the ley energy map, so we can do further analysis.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Is it able to simulate the critters, too?

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Certainly. Simulating critters is lesson one in the ley line textbook.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: We can use the simulation to carry out targeted training against the critters.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Looks like the study of ley lines is more organized than I thought.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Congratulations, Comrade Windsong. You will have the manpower you need.
Windsong turns as more and more fists are raised into the air.

items.speaker: Resident I
items.text: Turn it on, comrade!

items.speaker: Resident II
items.text: We can't wait!
A deep breath, a glance to confirm that all is ready, then ...
*click*

items.speaker: "Kikituk"
items.text: *roars*
Evgeni instinctively positions himself in front of everyone.

items.speaker: Knut
items.text: Hahahaha, it's like digging the mine all over again!

items.speaker: The Other Resident
items.text: That was the biggest achievement of my life!

items.speaker: Knut
items.text: Let's do this, comrades!

items.speaker: Knut
items.text: Digging like this is no easy work!
They roll up their sleeves, pressing forward confidently.

items.speaker: Knut
items.text: Phew! That was one powerful blow. Hahahahaha!
The square is now pocked by groups of disheveled workers, resting after their rigorous exertion.
Windsong's back is soaked, and her simulator creaks with stress.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: I think we can draw our conclusions now.
*creak*
The old bench groans beneath her boots as she nimbly propels herself onto its narrow back.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Everyone! We have to admit this is going to be a risky operation, but it's also our last chance.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: To protect our land and our people!

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: We must explore the mine!

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: There will be danger; yes, some of us may get hurt, but we may also find this new resource and save our Rayashki.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: For you, for me, for everyone!
There is no cheer that rises to meet her. The only thing audible now is the distant sea breeze buffeting the shore.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: We can already expect that critters have occupied the mine. We'll just have to work together to drive them away!

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: We dug this mine with our old machines once, and we'll do it again!

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: This is how we've made it so far.
The crowd rises, pulling in together. Windsong looks up and outward.

items.speaker: Knut
items.text: However old they are now, they will always be our children, right?

items.speaker: Knut
items.text: Yuri, you are good at assembling, huh? Nikita, you're going to be busy with the engines. Valeriya, we need you for the screws!
More and more stars light up.
They outshine the twinkling snow.
